answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can influence a market or vote. The protocol caps influence per deposit and destroys part of it when independent evidence shows coordinated fraud, so creating a thousand names does not create a thousand free votes. A sybil operator must tie up real capital for every identity and risks losing it; the burden is like hauling shale across a tundra, while a vine of linked accounts still shares the same costly root.
